summary: Explains `ansible-galaxy collection list`, which shows installed collections per search path with versions (`*` when unknown), including in-development collections with only `galaxy.yml`. Warns to only use directly installed collections, not ones pulled in as dependencies, and shows how to list one collection by FQCN.
questions: How do I see which collections are installed?
Why does a collection show * as its version?
How do I check where a specific collection is installed and which version?
Why do I see collections I never installed in the list?
How can I get more detail from ansible-galaxy collection list?

answer_card.title: List installed collections
answer_card.answer_md:
Run `ansible-galaxy collection list` to see every installed collection in the configured search paths, grouped by path with version numbers. Collections under development that have a `galaxy.yml` instead of `MANIFEST.json` show too; if no version info is available the version shows as `*`. Add `-vvv` for more detail.

To see all instances of one collection, pass its FQCN:

```bash
ansible-galaxy collection list fortinet.fortios
```

You may see collections that were installed as dependencies; only use collections in playbooks that you installed directly.
